claims.text: A near-equiatomic Hf20Mo20Ta20Ti20Zr20 alloy can achieve room-temperature yield strength above 1200 MPa.
A near-equiatomic Hf20Mo20Ta20Ti20Zr20 alloy can achieve room-temperature tensile elongation above 15%.
Solutionizing above the B2 order-disorder transition, quenching, and aging can create a continuous disordered BCC matrix containing discrete nanoscale B2 precipitates.
The B2 order-disorder transition temperature of Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr is estimated to be 1300-1450 °C.
Aging at 600-800 °C for 10-50 hours will precipitate nanoscale B2 particles in the Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr BCC matrix.
The proposed B2 precipitates will be enriched in Ti and Zr, while the matrix will be enriched in Mo, Ta, and Hf.
A continuous disordered BCC matrix provides sufficient plastic deformation capability to improve ductility.
Discrete B2 precipitates impede dislocation motion and thereby provide precipitation strengthening.
Inverting the phase topology avoids a continuous brittle B2 network and can combine higher ductility with high strength.
A continuous ordered B2 network is the primary cause of brittleness in the proposed as-cast alloy.
Reducing Hf and Ta and increasing the relative amount of Ti or Zr can lower alloy density while preserving the required BCC/B2 phase balance.
The optimized alloy will have a room-temperature yield strength of 1200-1400 MPa.
The optimized alloy will have a room-temperature tensile elongation of 15-25%.
The optimized alloy will have a density of 10.5-11.5 g/cm³.
The equiatomic Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr baseline has a density of approximately 12.5 g/cm³.
As-cast equiatomic Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr typically has yield strength above 1500 MPa and ductility below 5%.
The approach requires a single-phase BCC or BCC+B2 field at the solutionizing temperature.
Formation of TCP phases or retention of a continuous B2 network would prevent the proposed strength-ductility combination.
Excessive grain growth or B2 precipitate coarsening would reduce strength.

The hypothesis is falsified if an inverted microstructure fails to deliver more than 15% elongation, if density cannot be reduced by more than 3% while retaining strength above 1000 MPa and ductility, or if heat treatment produces continuous B2 or TCP phases.

contradictions.description: The stated density reductions are numerically inconsistent. Relative to the stated 12.5 g/cm³ baseline, 10.5-11.5 g/cm³ corresponds to an approximately 8-16% reduction, not the claimed 5-8% or 5-10% range.
